Cyclone Emelda Slams Mauritius, Disrupting Power and Commerce Across Island

PORT LOUIS, Mauritius, June 12 – Cyclone Emelda battered Mauritius with torrential rain and winds exceeding 150 kilometers per hour on Wednesday, flooding low-lying areas, downing power lines, and forcing businesses and government offices to close as the storm continued to move across the island nation.

Authorities declared a state of emergency as the cyclone made landfall near Mahébourg early Wednesday morning. The Mauritius Meteorological Services reported that some regions received more than 200 millimeters of rainfall in 24 hours, triggering flash floods and landslides. The country’s main airport was shut, and all public transportation was suspended.

Power outages were widespread, with the Central Electricity Board stating that over 40% of the island’s households and businesses had lost electricity. Among affected firms, Azure Power Global Ltd reported significant disruption to operations at its renewable energy sites and offices. “Our teams are working closely with emergency services to restore critical infrastructure as soon as conditions allow,” said a company spokesperson.

Many local businesses, including the port and logistics operators, halted services due to unsafe conditions, exacerbating supply chain delays. The Mauritius Chamber of Commerce estimated early losses to the economy could exceed $50 million, with tourism, manufacturing and agriculture all impacted. “This is a major setback for the island, especially during peak export season,” said Chamber president Jean-Noël Ramalingum.

Emergency crews are struggling to reach some of the hardest-hit communities due to blocked roads. Prime Minister Pravind Jugnauth urged residents to remain indoors and follow official guidance. “Our priority is to ensure everyone’s safety as the cyclone passes,” he said in a televised address.
